e a better value. All 27 instances certify above the Bernoulli lower bound. Each `strategy` call takes at most 0.1 s on the training set, and n=12 takes 0.6 s.

**How it works (`strategy.py`)**
- For fixed weights, the best atoms sit at a corner of the region {0 ≤ xᵢ ≤ 1, c·x ≤ t}. Moving atoms down only adds sums that are ≤ t.
- The strategy finds all 3-atom corners with exact integer arithmetic. For each corner, it searches the middle weight (grid, then a golden-section refinement).
- It also tests the 2-point laws in closed form: {t/n, 1}, {0, t/J} and {(t−J)/(n−J), 1}.
- The checker's repair step recomputes the last two weights, so the mean is exactly m.

**Results**

| Laws found | Instances |
|---|---|
| {t/n, 1} | 15 |
| {(t−J)/(n−J), 1} or {0, t/J} | 11 |
| {0, 9/10, 1} (3 atoms) | `n6_m3-5_t9-10`: 0.017904, compared with 0.017833 for the best 2-point law |

**Checks for more atoms**

| Search | Result |
|---|---|
| 4-atom corners (all of them, numpy, outside the strategy) | no gain on any instance |
| 5-atom random local search | falls back to the same laws on every instance |
| n=1 | gives (1−m)/(1−t), the known answer |
| Integer t (n=8, 10, 12) | Bernoulli is the best law found |

**`report.json`**: 0.85 for n=3, 0.8 for n=4, 0.7 for n=6, and 0.6 for the 3-atom n=6 instance. I did not prove that any of these values is optimal. Laws with 5 or more atoms were only tested with the local search, so they are not excluded. That is why the numbers are lower for larger n.
